hunks.title: Hash passwords with salted scrypt and compare in constant time
hunks.explanation: scrypt is memory-hard and salted per user, so identical passwords no longer share a hash and rainbow tables stop working. timingSafeEqual removes the string-compare timing channel. No new dependency: it ships with Node.

thr-002.question: Where should tokens live in the browser, and how should refresh tokens behave?

options.title: httpOnly refresh cookie + in-memory access token, with rotation
options.summary: Login sets a Secure, httpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie carrying the refresh token. The access token lives only in memory and expires in 15 minutes. Every refresh issues a new refresh token and revokes the old one.
pros: Reuse of an old refresh token detects theft
Short access TTL bounds the damage of a leak
cons: Needs a small store of issued refresh token ids
CORS must move back to an explicit origin list with credentials
Requires a CSRF story for the refresh endpoint

options.title: Keep localStorage, add rotation and a 15-minute access TTL
options.summary: Smallest change to the current code: rotate refresh tokens on every use, cut the access TTL, remove the console.log. Storage stays where it is.
pros: Two small server changes and one client change
cons: Refresh token still readable by any script on the origin
A single XSS still yields a long-lived session

options.title: Sliding-window refresh token, no rotation
options.summary: Each refresh extends the expiry of the same refresh token. Simplest possible server logic.
pros: No concurrency issues on the client
cons: A stolen refresh token works alongside the real one indefinitely

hunks.title: Scope DELETE to the caller's own favorites
hunks.explanation: Passing the caller's userId lets the store refuse foreign ids. Returning 404 rather than 403 avoids confirming that the id exists.

hunks.title: Check ownership in the store
hunks.explanation: The store is the last line of defence: even a future route that forgets the check cannot delete across users.

hunks.title: Validate the create body with a strict schema
hunks.explanation: Bounds coordinates and string lengths and rejects unknown properties before anything reaches the store or an upstream URL. Needs `import { z } from 'zod'` and `badRequest` from lib/errors.

hunks.title: Fail at startup when JWT_SECRET is missing
hunks.explanation: Production boots refuse to run with a missing or short secret. Development keeps a default, but only outside production and with a visible warning.

hunks.title: Accept the token from the Authorization header only
hunks.explanation: Removes the ?token= path so bearer credentials never appear in URLs, logs, history or Referer headers. Also replaces indexOf == 0 with startsWith.

edges.note: Calls the provider directly, once per favorite, skipping the TtlCache used by routes/forecast

thr-005.explanation: Today the two stores depend on each other and a route reaches past the cache into the provider. With a service layer, the cascade delete lives in services/accounts, favorites enrichment goes through the same cached forecast lookup the forecast route uses, and every edge points in one direction: routes to services to stores and providers.

children.title: Ordering hazard
children.text: The new web build sends an Authorization header on every request. The API currently in production does not allow that header in CORS preflight. If the web app ships first, every forecast and geocode call fails and the app goes blank for signed-in users.

steps.title: Provision JWT_SECRET in dev, staging and prod
steps.description: At least 32 random bytes per environment. Without it the API silently signs tokens with the default committed to the repo.

steps.title: Make the API refuse to boot without the secret
steps.description: Turn the fallback into a startup error so a missing value fails the deploy instead of shipping the dev secret.

steps.title: Deploy the API
steps.description: CORS allows Authorization from the explicit web origin, auth and favorites routes are live, nothing calls them yet.

steps.title: Deploy the web app with the accounts UI behind a flag, off
steps.description: The bundle ships dark. Existing users see no change and no Authorization header is sent until the flag is on.

steps.title: Flip the flag and watch 401 and CORS error rates
steps.description: One switch to roll back if the auth flow misbehaves, no redeploy needed.

rows: CORS preflight rejects Authorization; all data requests fail
Tokens signed with the public default; anyone can mint one
Login form posts to routes that return 404

hunks.title: Retry once after refresh and make refresh single-flight
hunks.explanation: The retried flag bounds the recursion to one retry. refreshOnce shares a single in-flight promise so concurrent 401s wait for the same refresh instead of racing and overwriting each other.

hunks.title: Decode the JWT payload as base64url and survive bad tokens
hunks.explanation: JWT segments are base64url. Converting to standard base64 with padding makes atob safe, and the try/catch turns a stale or malformed token into a signed-out state instead of a crash on mount.

annotations.author: sentinel-bot
annotations.text: Emails are stored and compared exactly as typed, so Ada@Example.com and ada@example.com become two accounts. Normalise with trim().toLowerCase() on register and login.

annotations.author: sentinel-bot
annotations.text: No rate limiting, lockout or delay on login. With the fast hash this makes credential stuffing cheap. Add a per-IP and per-email limiter and return 429 with Retry-After.

annotations.author: sentinel-bot
annotations.text: Distinct messages for unknown email and wrong password reveal which emails are registered. Return one generic 401 for both branches.

thr-009.question: How should the favorites panel stay in sync across devices?

options.title: Refetch on focus and visibility, plus after local mutations
options.summary: Reload the list when the tab regains focus or becomes visible, and after every add or remove. No timer at all.
pros: Covers the "added it on my phone" case the moment the user returns
A few lines in the existing hook
cons: Changes made while the tab is already focused on another device appear only on the next focus

options.title: Poll with backoff, paused while hidden
options.summary: Keep the interval but start at 60 seconds, pause when document.hidden, and reset on user activity.
cons: Timer and visibility bookkeeping to maintain

options.title: Server push over Server-Sent Events
options.summary: The favorites route exposes an event stream and pushes changes to every connected client for that user.
cons: New long-lived connection to run and scale
Auth for the stream needs its own design
Heavy for a list that changes a few times a day

thr-010.title: Line coverage of code touched by this PR
thr-010.note: The one new test exercises register and login only. Every 0% row is a file with no test at all, and the untested branches include the security-relevant ones flagged in other threads. The repo has no web test setup yet, so the web rows need a harness before they can move.
